title: What does the PSPF require for security awareness training?
description: What PSPF Release 2026 requires for security awareness training: Requirements 0024, 0025 and 0219, who they apply to, and how to evidence them.
shortAnswer: The Protective Security Policy Framework (PSPF) Release 2026 requires non-corporate Commonwealth entities to provide security awareness training to all personnel, including contractors, at engagement and annually thereafter (Requirement 0024), and targeted security training for specialist or high-risk positions (Requirement 0025). From 1 July 2026, awareness training must also cover foreign interference, espionage, cultivation and exploitation by foreign powers (Requirement 0219).
keyTakeaways: PSPF Release 2026, published by the Department of Home Affairs, took effect on 1 July 2026 and is organised into six domains with numbered requirements.
Requirement 0024: security awareness training at engagement and annually, for personnel including contractors.
Requirement 0025: targeted training for personnel in specialist or high-risk positions.
Requirement 0219 (new, 1 July 2026): awareness training must cover foreign interference, espionage, cultivation and exploitation by foreign powers.
Accountable Authorities report PSPF compliance annually to their minister and to Home Affairs, so training evidence must stand up to reporting.
regulator: Department of Home Affairs (PSPF policy owner)
appliesTo: Non-corporate Commonwealth entities under the PGPA Act (mandatory)
Corporate Commonwealth entities and wholly-owned Commonwealth companies (better practice)
Contractors and service providers bound by PSPF terms in their contracts

sections.heading: Who must comply with the PSPF training requirements?

blocks.text: Non-corporate Commonwealth entities must comply. The [PSPF Release 2026](https://www.protectivesecurity.gov.au/system/files/2026-07/pspf-release-2026_6.pdf) states that these entities must apply the PSPF in accordance with section 21 of the Public Governance, Performance and Accountability Act 2013 (PGPA Act), under the Minister for Home Affairs' Directive on the Security of Government Business. For corporate Commonwealth entities and wholly-owned Commonwealth companies, the PSPF represents better practice.

The training requirements explicitly include contractors. Entities also flow PSPF obligations to service providers through contract terms, so suppliers working with Commonwealth information often need to show equivalent training records. For the technical cyber layer that sits beneath the PSPF, see the companion page on the [ISM and cyber security awareness training](/regulations/ism-cyber-security-awareness-training).

sections.heading: Which version of the PSPF is current?

blocks.text: As at September 2026, the current version is PSPF Release 2026, with a publication date of 1 July 2026. The Department of Home Affairs now publishes the PSPF as an annual release, and [announced Release 2026](https://www.protectivesecurity.gov.au/news/pspf-release-2026-now-available) as introducing policy improvements on emerging technologies, including training on artificial intelligence (AI) use, and training on countering foreign interference.

The framework has five tiers: principles, protective security domains, policy (the mandatory requirements), standards and technical manuals, and guidelines. The six domains are Governance, Risk, Information, Technology, Personnel and Physical. Each requirement carries a permanent number, a domain, an applicability marker and the date it was last updated, which makes it straightforward to cite individual requirements in a training register.

sections.heading: What exactly do the training requirements say?

blocks.text: Three Governance domain requirements in section 3.5 set the training baseline, and several requirements in other domains add targeted briefings. The core wording is short and decisive.

blocks.text: Release 2026 also strengthened Requirement 0050 so that personnel do not publicise their security clearance level on online platforms, including employment-focused platforms such as LinkedIn, and added Requirement 0220 requiring a specific policy prohibiting such publication. These are policy requirements rather than training requirements, but they create content that awareness training has to carry.

sections.heading: What should PSPF security awareness training cover?

blocks.text: It should cover the entity's own protective security practices and the threats relevant to each person's role. Section 3.5 of the PSPF lists what makes awareness training effective, including that it:

items: is championed and practised by senior leadership
delivers an ongoing awareness program that regularly reminds individuals of security responsibilities, issues and concerns
briefs personnel on the access privileges and prohibitions attached to their clearance level before access is given
ensures personnel with specific security duties receive appropriate and up-to-date training
clearly communicates the entity's protective security practices and procedures to all personnel, including contractors
gives all personnel a clear understanding of the security environment and the threats relevant to their roles

blocks.text: For Requirement 0219, section 3.5.1 identifies four topics: what foreign interference and espionage are, recognising them, recognising cultivation and exploitation by a foreign actor, and the security risks of disclosing clearance details on online platforms.

sections.heading: How do you evidence PSPF training compliance?

blocks.text: Evidence must show timing (at engagement, then annually), coverage (all personnel including contractors), and content (the 0219 topics from 1 July 2026). Accountable Authorities report PSPF compliance annually to their minister and to Home Affairs, and Home Affairs quality assures those reports, so the evidence needs to be retrievable by requirement number.

blocks.text: A register built this way is easier to maintain when the PSPF changes each July. The broader method is covered in [how to report training compliance to the board](/guides/how-to-report-training-compliance-to-the-board) and [how to update training when regulations change](/guides/how-to-update-training-when-regulations-change).

sections.heading: How should training keep up with annual PSPF releases?

blocks.text: Review training content against each July release and its summary of changes. Home Affairs publishes a [summary of changes for Release 2026](https://www.protectivesecurity.gov.au/publications-library/pspf-release-2026-summary-changes) that lists each new or amended requirement by section and number, which is the natural trigger list for a content review.

items: On release, extract every new or amended requirement that affects personnel behaviour.
Map each to the modules and assessment items that depend on it.
Update content, re-version it, and record the requirement number and release year against the change.
Decide whether existing completions remain valid or whether a top-up module is needed before the next annual cycle.
Keep the previous version, so completions can be traced to the content that was in force at the time.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry treats each PSPF requirement as a numbered source linked to the concepts and assessment points it drives. When a new release adds or changes a requirement, the dependent content and assessment items are identified for review, and the provenance record shows which release each version of the training reflects.

faqs.q: Does the PSPF say how long security awareness training must be?
faqs.a: No. Requirement 0024 sets timing and audience, at engagement and annually for personnel including contractors, but not duration or format. The PSPF guidance focuses on content and effectiveness, such as leadership support, role relevance and regular reminders, so entities decide format based on their risk environment.

faqs.q: Do contractors need PSPF security awareness training?
faqs.a: Yes. Requirements 0024 and 0025 both refer to personnel, including contractors. Entities commonly include the obligation in contract terms and require the provider to supply completion evidence, or enrol contractors in the entity's own program at engagement.

faqs.q: When did the foreign interference training requirement start?
faqs.a: Requirement 0219 carries a date of 1 July 2026 in PSPF Release 2026. It requires security awareness training to cover foreign interference, espionage, cultivation and exploitation by foreign powers. Entities should check that the annual module delivered after that date covers the four topics listed in section 3.5.1.

faqs.q: Is the PSPF the same as the ISM?
faqs.a: No. The PSPF is Home Affairs policy covering governance, risk, information, technology, personnel and physical security. The Information Security Manual (ISM) is the Australian Signals Directorate's cyber security framework. PSPF requirements refer to the ISM for cyber security, and the ISM has its own awareness training controls.
